Portfolio case study by Rupak Ghanpathi · built solo · sample data
A distributor pays short. On day 31 it's still nobody's problem.

Every Rupee is a short-payment reconciliation desk for FMCG finance teams, built from Cello World's public filings. Every gap gets one owner and ends in a credit note or a recovery.

Try the live desk
Talk to Rupak

The hard part of a deduction isn't matching it. It's owning it.

The call I made: control over speed. No auto write-offs, maker-checker above ₹10,000, strict matching at launch. Fewer auto-matches and more manual work, on purpose.

THE PART NOBODY OWNS

A deduction can have a tax deadline.

When a brand settles a scheme claim with a GST credit note, it gets back the GST already paid on the discount. That credit note must go out by 30 November after the financial year ends (or the annual return date, if earlier). For FY 2025-26 supplies, that's 30 November 2026.

Many brands settle schemes with a plain financial credit note instead and keep the GST cost. From 1 Nov 2026 the GST route gets easier, so more claims will qualify. An undecided deduction quietly loses that choice after the deadline.

The brand's GST gain is the distributor's input-credit reversal. That's why the two sides negotiate which kind of credit note gets issued.

CGST Act s.34(2); s.15(3)(b) as amended by Finance Act 2026; CBIC Circular 251/08/2025. Summarised from public sources, Oct 2026. Not tax advice.

Costs, mistakes, risks
What this design costs, what I got wrong, and where it could fail.
+
What this costs
Fewer auto-matches at launch: strict matching rejects fuzzy ones.
More manual review: anything above ₹10,000 needs a second person.
A slower first close: Sales must enter scheme dates and budgets before rules can accept a claim.

What I got wrong: v2 was a wall of text, so I rebuilt it as something you can run, because a spec nobody executes isn't a spec.

How I'd work from week one
Evidence first. Every fact dated and sourced.
One owner per gap. One decision, one deadline.
Testable rules. 16 rules, 31 tests, "must block" cases included.
Controls built in. Maker-checker, no auto write-offs. Zero SOX findings at HDFC.
Where it could fail, and the fix
Distributors pay the old account. Keep it open a quarter; Sales gets a weekly list.
Schemes change mid-quarter. No dates and budget from Sales, no valid scheme.
Sales overrides the credit flag. It never blocks an order; overrides are logged by name.
Runs in your browser. Uploaded files never leave your device.
No sign-up, no tracking.
Sample data only.
Sources, and what I don't claim

THE PART NOBODY OWNS

A deduction can have a tax deadline.

When a brand settles a scheme claim with a GST credit note, it gets back the GST already paid on the discount. That credit note must go out by 30 November after the financial year ends (or the annual return date, if earlier). For FY 2025-26 supplies, that's 30 November 2026.

Many brands settle schemes with a plain financial credit note instead and keep the GST cost. From 1 Nov 2026 the GST route gets easier, so more claims will qualify. An undecided deduction quietly loses that choice after the deadline.

The brand's GST gain is the distributor's input-credit reversal. That's why the two sides negotiate which kind of credit note gets issued.

CGST Act s.34(2); s.15(3)(b) as amended by Finance Act 2026; CBIC Circular 251/08/2025. Summarised from public sources, Oct 2026. Not tax advice.

+
What this costs
Fewer auto-matches at launch: strict matching rejects fuzzy ones.
More manual review: anything above ₹10,000 needs a second person.
A slower first close: Sales must enter scheme dates and budgets before rules can accept a claim.

What I got wrong: v2 was a wall of text, so I rebuilt it as something you can run, because a spec nobody executes isn't a spec.

How I'd work from week one
Evidence first. Every fact dated and sourced.
One owner per gap. One decision, one deadline.
Testable rules. 16 rules, 31 tests, "must block" cases included.
Controls built in. Maker-checker, no auto write-offs. Zero SOX findings at HDFC.
Where it could fail, and the fix
Distributors pay the old account. Keep it open a quarter; Sales gets a weekly list.
Schemes change mid-quarter. No dates and budget from Sales, no valid scheme.
Sales overrides the credit flag. It never blocks an order; overrides are logged by name.
Runs in your browser. Uploaded files never leave your device.
No sign-up, no tracking.
